description: Pudge затягивает своих жертв в смертельный капкан «Meat Hook», затем наращивает урон чередой кровавых ударов «Rot». Его «Dismember» позволяет надолго обездвижить врага, превращая его в простую добычу. Он безжалостен в выслеживании одиночных целей и способен перевернуть исход дуэли.

title: Pugna
description: In the realm of Pugna's birth, near the vents of the Nether Reaches, there stood a school of sorcery that lost its headmaster to an unfortunate 'accident'. Seizing this chance, Pugna, then a master of oblivity artes, proclaimed himself the new head of school. Under his administration, the academy's curriculum shifted toward the dark arts, and the grounds became a twisted warren of unholy experiments. When the Nether Lords heard of Pugna's ascent, they laughed, for they knew that a creature of pure voidstuff like Pugna could not help but attract the attention of the greater demons. And so it was that Pugna's school was besieged by hellish forces seeking to claim his soul. Pugna fought, but soon found himself overmatched. To save his school (and his skin), he unleashed the forbidden Nether Blast, instantly disintegrating a score of fiends. The blast had an unexpected side effect, however: it opened a rift to another dimension. From this rift issued an endless swarm of astral spirits, which Pugna commanded to repel the invaders. As the demons fled, Pugna's heart filled with glee. He had found a source of power that was infinite, and that obeyed his every command. With the spirits at his side, Pugna became a force to be reckoned with, and he now travels the planes, seeking new victims for his endless hunger.

title: Razor
description: Among the emblem walking of the lightning revenants, one survives immemorial. A once-great power reduced to slavery by the Narrow Maze, Razor knows endless indignation. Imprisoned for an age without recourse, he seethes with fury at his helplessness, lashing out at all who pass through his labyrinth of electrified walls. To Razor the Lightning Revenant, the Narrow Maze is an especially cruel prison - for a creature of pure electrical energy, it is a place that both starves and confines him. He spends his days desperately seeking a way out, lashing out at other trapped souls with bolts of lightning that serve only to further weaken him. His plasma blasts drain his essence, but they are his only means of escape. For the day he finds the exit, he will be completely drained - a weak and易 victim for the first denizen of the Underscape he encounters. But Razor is patient. He waits, eyes gleaming in the dark, for the day when he can finally escape his prison and seek vengeance on those who trapped him there.

title: Riki
description: Riki was born middle child to the great dynasty of Tahlin. With an older brother groomed for the throne, and a younger brother expected to some day be the Captain of the Guard, Riki's options were limited. He honed his skills in the shadows, silently eliminating threats to the royal family and becoming the perfect spy. But on the night of his greatest triumph - with the entire Tahlin family poisoned during a celebratory dinner - he discovered that the toxin used came from the royal merchant's stores, and that the merchant had disappeared. Riki continues to serve the royal line, but his methods have changed. No longer a spy, he seeks now to avenge the Tahlin family and bring justice to those who would dare harm his people. His tools are stealth and surprise, and his calling is that of the assassin.

title: Rubick
description: Any mage can cast a spell or two, and a few may even study long enough to become a wizard, but only the most talented are allowed to be recognized as a Magus. Yet as with any sorcerer's circle, a sense of community has never guaranteed competitive courtesy. Already a renowned duelist and scholar of the grander world of sorcery, it had never occurred to Rubick that he might perhaps be Magus material until he was in the midst of his seventh assassination attempt. As he casually tossed the twelfth of a string of would-be killers from a high balcony, it dawned on him how utterly unimaginative the attempts on his life had become. Where once the interruption of a fingersnap or firehand might have put a cheerful spring in his step, it had all become so very predictable. He craved greater competition. Therefore, donning his combat mask, he did what any wizard seeking to ascend the ranks would do: he announced his intention to kill a Magus. Rubick quickly discovered that to threaten one Magus is to threaten them all, and they fell upon him in force. Each antagonist's spell was an unstoppable torrent of energy, and every attack a calculated killing blow. But very soon something occurred that Rubick's foes found unexpected: their arts appeared to turn against them. Inside the magic maelstrom, Rubick chuckled, subtly reading and replicating the powers of one in order to cast it against another, sowing chaos among those who had allied against him. Accusations of betrayal began to fly, and soon the sorcerers turned one upon another without suspecting who was behind their undoing. When the battle finally drew to a close, all were singed and frozen, soaked and cut and pierced. More than one lay dead by an ally's craft. Rubick stood apart, sore but delighted in the week's festivities. None had the strength to argue when he presented his petition of assumption to the Hidden Council, and the Insubstantial Eleven agreed as one to grant him the title of Grand Magus.

title: Sand King
description: The sands of the Scintillant Waste are alive and sentient--the whole vast desert speaks to itself, thinking thoughts only such a vastness can conceive. But when it needs must find a form to communicate with those of more limited scope, it frees a fragment of itself, and fills a carapace of magic armor formed by the cunning Djinn of Qaldin. This essential identity calls itself Crixalis, meaning 'Soul of the Sand', but others know it as Sand King. Sand King takes the form of a huge arachnid, inspired by the Scintillant Waste's small but ubiquitous denizens; and this is a true outward expression of his ferocious nature. Guardian, warrior, ambassador--Sand King is all of these things, inseparable from the endless desert that gave him life.

title: Shadow Demon
description: Among the sovereign Demons with explicit access to this world, Doom scarcely bothers with the affairs of Noninfernals and Lesser Spectral Consorts, while Shadow Fiend passes through almost exclusively on collecting expeditions. The Shadow Demon, however, has always taken a deep and abiding interest in the material plane, as if sensing that mastery of this gritty dimensional nexus might be the key to total domination of all realities. Summoned first by minor wizards, the Shadow Demon granted every wish and put on increasingly impressive displays of power until he had the full attention of the greatest demonologists, and through them the various lords, tyrants, autarchs and heirophants who depended on sorcery to buttress their mundane power. So great was his deception that all his summoners considered themselves the master and Shadow Demon the servant; meanwhile, he eroded their identities and made their minds his own. In the end, most members of the cult were hollow puppets, extensions of his evil will. What Shadow Demon's next step would have been remains open to speculation, for around this time, Nevermore the Shadow Fiend bit into a particularly nasty-tasting soul and discovered that it held nothing but a foul nougat of Shadow Demon's essence. Alerted that a coup was underway, and that the ancient equilibrium of the Umbral Pact was about to be destabilized, Doom and Shadow Fiend briefly joined forces to destroy the burgeoning cult. Combining spells of incredible force, they undid Shadow Demon's centuries of patient work, reducing his cult to smithereens—and all its members to a bloody splatter. Nothing remained except a tiny speck of demon shadow. Immortal and irreducible, this mote of evil was enough to seed the Shadow Demon's next scheme, and in fits and starts, over further centuries, he began to regroup. Whatever that speck of shadow touched, it tainted, and its influence gradually grew. A chaos of damaged parts pulled together, reknit, and combined to give Shadow Demon a form even more alarming and unlikely than it had originally possessed. He has no name now, but those who survive his presence know him as the Shadow Demon. And they run from him in terror.

title: Shadow Shaman
text: Мастер проклятий и тотемов, искусно управляющий разумом врагов.
description: Shadow Shaman устанавливает «Serpent Wards», создающие невидимые охранные башни, и обрушивает на врагов «Hex», превращая их в беспомощных существ. Благодаря «Mass Serpent Ward» он может ломать башни и выдерживать натиск врагов, а сочетание контроля и урона делает его грозным магом поддержки.

title: Silencer
description: Part of the seventh and final generation of a carefully designed pedigree, Nortrom was bred by the ancient order of the Aeol Drias to be the greatest magic user the world had ever seen. He was the prophesied one, the culmination of two hundred years of careful pairings, a war-mage who would bring glory to the order, and destruction to their sworn enemies, the Knights of the Fold. Raised with other young mages in a monastical setting, Nortrom learned to control his abilities at a young age. He mastered the arts of telekinesis and bilocation, and could bend fire and ice to his will. But as he grew, so too did his pride, and he chafed under the strictures of the order. He dreamed of battle, of using his gifts to bring order to the world. When the Aeol Drias finally sent their greatest son forth, they expected him to return triumphant, leading the order into a golden age. But Nortrom never returned. Defeated by an unknown foe, he was spirited away, never to be seen again. The order searched for their lost son for generations, but eventually they gave up. The prophecy, it seemed, had failed. But the prophecy was not wrong--Nortrom had merely chosen a different path. Calling himself the Silencer, he dedicates himself not to the Aeol Drias, but to the pursuit of knowledge, and the mastery of magic. He seeks out those who would misuse their powers, and cuts them off from the source--silencing them forever.

title: Skywrath Mage
description: A highly placed mage in the Ghastly Eyrie, Dragonus lives a troubled existence. Sworn by birth to protect whoever sits on the Nest of Thorns, he hates the current Skywrath queen with all his soul. As a youth, he was favored by Scree'auk, the goddess who gave the Skywrath a form that could fly. But as he grew, he found himself increasingly at odds with the queen's politics, until the day came when he could stand no more. He stole away the grieving Vengeful Spirit, who had herself been betrayed by the queen, and together they plotted their revenge. But schemes against the vigilance of the Skywrath are not easily contrived, and the queen's mages soon learned of Dragonus' plot. They came for him in the night, and would have killed him if not for the intervention of Scree'auk. The goddess appeared to her favorite, and granted him wings with which to escape. But the gift came at a price: Scree'auk gave her form to empower Vengeful Spirit, and gave her life to empower Dragonus. Now he soars the skies in search of revenge against a queen he may once have loved. With the Skywrath Mage's magic at his command, and the Vengeful Spirit as his companion, he will not rest until he sees the queen's wings clipped, and the Ghastly Eyrie brought to heel.

title: Slark
description: Little known to the inhabitants of the dry world, Dark Reef is a very large prison complex inhabited by countless generations of its original detainees, along with their descendants. It is a deep water dungeon, built long ago by unknown hands. The prison is built in the carcass of some ancient leviathan, and the inmates are a mix of sea creatures and wayward land dwellers who wandered too far into the waves. The prison is self-sustaining, with inmates to fill every role from guards to wardens to magistrates. The only punishment for failure or disobedience is the Black Days--a judgment carried out in pitch darkness, where the screams of the guilty can be heard echoing through the halls. It is said that no one survives the Black Days, save for those who have mastered the art of stealth and cunning. Slark is one such creature. A cunning brute with no particular allegiance, he was captured while raiding a lake village, and thrown into Dark Reef. There he survived forty-three Black Days--a record. With each pronouncement of judgment he disappeared into the pitch black, and with each commutation he reappeared in his cell, alone and unmarked. At last the warden sent in all his best guards to execute the sentence--but Slark was not in his cell. He had disappeared without a trace, and has not been seen since. It is said that he now roams the land, a living blade of vengeance, cutting down those who would abuse their power, and leaving only silence in his wake.

title: Snapfire
description: Beadie and her dragon toad Mortimer are a traveling explosives show, entertaining crowds with feats of demolition and destruction. But when the pair get into hot water with a criminal gang, they find themselves far from home, navigating the outlaw backwoods on a quest for revenge. Small in stature but big on destruction, Beadie packs a wallop with her scatterblast shotgun and homemade cookies. And when things really heat up, she calls on her amphibian sidekick for a grand finale guaranteed to bring down the house.

title: Sniper
text: Виртуозный стрелок, поражающий цель с невероятной дистанции.
description: Sniper пользуется «Assassinate», чтобы нанести точный выстрел издалека, и «Shrapnel», чтобы замедлять и ранить группы противников. Его «Headshot» даёт шанс сбить цель с ног, а «Take Aim» увеличивает дальность стрельбы, превращая его в идеального снайпера командных стычек. 000 ,

title: Spectre
description: Just as higher states of energy seek a lower level, the Spectre known as Mercurial is a being of intense and violent energy who finds herself irresistibly drawn to scenes of strife as they unfold in the physical world. While her normal spectral state transcends sensory limitations, each time she takes on a physical manifestation, she is stricken by insatiable thirst. This thirst drives her to stalk the material plane, where she can quench her hunger upon the bodies of those less fortunate. It is believed that the intensity of her presence causes her features to wither and warp, leaving her a nameless faceless Spectre, bent on the ruination of all who stand in the way of her needs.

title: Spirit Breaker
description: Barathrum the Spirit Breaker is a lordly and powerful creature, a being of predatory cunning who knows neither mercy nor fear. Taken from his homeland to be a circus freak in the shows of Slom, Barathrum broke his chains and escaped his keepers, but he never forgot the pain of captivity. Now he roams the world, seeking his revenge on all who would enslave others. His ghostly charge strikes from nowhere, stunning his foes and breaking their spirits. He is a creature of few words, but those words are not to be ignored. For Barathrum has a message for the world, and he will deliver it with his fists.

title: Storm Spirit
description: Storm Spirit is literally a force of nature--the wild power of wind and weather, bottled in human form. And a boisterous, jovial, irrepressible form it is! As jolly as a favorite uncle, he injects every scene with crackling energy. But it was not always so, and there was tragedy in his creation. Generations ago, in the plains beyond the Wailing Mountains, a good people survived by selected harvest and diligence. Thunderkeg the Brewmaster was one of them. A journeyman to the great mystics of the order, he had mastered the arts of controlled spirits and providential intuition. Yet none had prepared him for the day of the storm. Black clouds gathered and roiled, and from their depths emerged a spirit of wind and weather, a skyborne godling born full of mischief and temerity. This was the Storm Spirit, and no sooner had he emerged than he clapped his eyes upon the Brewmaster's daughter, whom he decided to claim for his bride. The skyborne godling demanded the frightened maiden. The Brewmaster sought to divert him with libations. The maiden's mother brought forth the finest silks. But the Storm Spirit would not be dissuaded. At last the Brewmaster, seeing no other way to save his daughter, challenged the godling to a drinking contest. The Storm Spirit, amused, accepted the challenge. Keg after keg they drank, until the ground was soaked with beer and vomit. The Storm Spirit grew careless, even as the Brewmaster grew bold. When the godling passed out in a puddle, Thunderkeg cleaved him in twain with his ritual staff. The maiden was saved. But the Brewmaster looked upon the cloven godling with pity. He could not abide such a mess. With a mournful sigh, he gathered the sundered halves and poured them into his brewing keg. Adding a few special ingredients, he shook the keg until the godling's essence was preserved in liquid form. When he opened the keg, a new being emerged: the Storm Spirit as we know him today, a creature of pure energy, in the shape of a jovial pandaren. The Brewmaster had saved his daughter, and created a being of pure mirth. But the Storm Spirit's memory is long, and his power is great. When the mood takes him, he can still be a tempest. For he is the soul of the storm, and though he may laugh, he is far from always jolly.

title: Sven
description: Sven is the bastard son of a Vigil Knight, born of a Pallid Meranth, raised in the Shadeshore Ruins. With his father executed for violating the Vigil Codes, and his mother shunned by her wild race, Sven believes that honor is to be found in no social order, but only in himself. After tending his mother through a lingering death, he offered himself as a novice to the Vigil Knights, never revealing his identity. For thirteen years he studied in his father's school, mastering the rigid code that declared his existence an abomination. Then, on the day that should have been his In-Swearing, he seized the Outcast Blade, shattered the Sacred Helm, and burned the Codex in the Vigil's Holy Flame. The Vigil Knights, now without their Iron Will, were no match for Sven's rage. He marched forth from the Vigil Keep, forever solitary, following his private code to the last perfect fulfillment.

title: Techies
description: In the chemistry of the mad bombardier, the cute exterior belies the volatile madness staring back. Squee, Spleen, and Spoon, the Techies Demolitions trio, have a reputation for being as brilliant as they are fragile. The goblins' small size belies their great ambition—to blow stuff up. Preferring to detonate their way out of trouble, the Techies have demolished countless landscapes in fits of gleeful gigglefits. But it's not all in fun. For the Techies are on a mission—to rid the world of 'dull' by reducing it to smoldering rubble. And with an arsenal of bombs, mines, and traps at their disposal, not to mention their signature explosive-equipped Kablooey Cart, the Techies are well equipped for the task.

title: Templar Assassin
description: Lanaya, the Templar Assassin, came to her calling by way of the Hidden Temple. For the Hidden Ones believe in no gods, but place their trust in secret knowledge, and it is that knowledge that she seeks. The Temple does not divulge its secrets easily, and to gain entrance she had to pass through many dangers, fighting guardians and evading traps. But Lanaya proved herself worthy, and the temple opened to her. Now she studies its lore, and the Hidden Temple has taught her much. It has taught her to move like light, to strike like shadow, to conceal herself in plain sight. And most of all, it has taught her to be patient, for the temple's greatest secrets are not won in a day, or even a year. But Lanaya knows that with time, all secrets will be revealed to her. And so she waits.

title: Terrorblade
description: Terrorblade is the twin brother of the Anti-Mage. Both of Night Elf Descent, Terrorblade was drawn in by the powers of the Undead, plunging into the depths of the Abyss, where he was forever changed. Now a demon marauder, he haunts the plains, ambushing the unwary and crushing all who oppose him. His understanding of soul manipulation allows him to take control of enemy forces, and when his foes strike at him, they end up cutting down their own allies. Those who witness his outcast form are driven mad with fright, for they see a reflection of their own fears. And when Terrorblade's gaze falls upon them, they are overcome with terror, as he forces them to confront their deepest fears. It is a poor soul indeed who is subject to Terrorblade's reflections.

title: Tidehunter
text: Безмолвный гигант из глубин моря, обрушивающий на врагов разрушительные волны.
description: Tidehunter вызывает мощный прилив «Anchor Smash», уменьшая урон от атак противников и нанося им урон. Его ультимативная способность «Ravage» отправляет вокруг себя спирали океана, оглушая и замедляя всех врагов в большом радиусе, что делает его идеальным инициатором командных боёв.

title: Timbersaw
description: Rizzrack could hardly be considered a villain, but the whole matter had left the keen tinker with something of a chip on his shoulder. Like his father before him, Rizzrack was not the sort to let a simple chip lie. So when the rumors reached his ears of a mighty tree that had stood for a thousand years, a tree whose wood was so strong that no blade could cut it, Rizzrack knew he had found his material. Packing up his things, he set out immediately. But upon seeing the tree for himself, he felt something strange. A kinship. The tree, it seemed, was alive in a way he had never seen before. Alive, and suffering. For the tree was anxious, and it spoke to Rizzrack of the source of its anxiety. The Rift. The Rift had been opened, and its influence had upset the balance of nature. The tree could sense it. And in turn, Rizzrack could sense the tree's pain. He vowed then to close the Rift, to save the tree and the forest. But to do so, he would need a suit of armor unlike any other. A suit that could channel the power of nature itself. And so, with the tree's blessing, Rizzrack set to work, using his skills to fashion a suit of living armor. The tree gave freely of its wood, and Rizzrack crafted it with care. When it was done, he donned the armor, and felt the power of the forest flow into him. He was ready. The Rift awaited.

title: Tinker
description: Boush the Tinker's diminutive race is known for its intelligence, its cunning, and its prickly relationship with magic. As a matter of pride, they survive by their wits, and use only those powers of nature that may be unlocked through rational methodologies. Even this forbearance has led to a series of bloody and bitter wars, as the Gougers' aggregation of natural lore has given them access to almost totemistic powers over life and death. When time came for Boush to conduct his own trials, he witnessed the same bloody equinox of war that had marked his people's own history, and decided that the old ways were an anachronism. He was dismissed from the tribe for his radical thinking, and left to his own devices. But the Tinkers do not give up easily, and Boush returned to his people a hero, proving his skills in battle against impossible foes with nothing but his wits and a few homemade contraptions. Now he uses his knowledge to serve no lord, and bounties collected from the heads of his enemies finance his research, which often results in explosive--often unpredictable--consequences.

title: Tiny
description: Coming to life as a chunk of stone, Tiny's bloodthirsty nature soon found him traveling the world in search of fights. The mountain he calls home seems to follow him on these journeys, as he gathers ever more pieces of the world to add to his frame. He carries with him an enormous tree, which serves as a suitable weapon for one of his stature. Ever hungry for battle, Tiny wanders the world, wasting away enemies with his tree and adding their essence to his rocky frame. With every fight, Tiny grows.

title: Treant Protector
description: Far to the west, in the mountains beyond the Vale of Augury, lies a sleepy town. It is said that the people there are so friendly, and the land so fertile, that no one ever leaves. But this is not entirely true. Long ago, a young elf named Rooftrellen wandered into the town, seeking adventure. The townsfolk welcomed him, and he stayed for a time, but eventually the call of the road drew him on. He said his farewells, and departed, but as he walked, he found the road growing faint, then vanishing altogether. He turned back, but the town was gone, as if it had never been. Confused, he headed into the woods, and there he remained. For the enchantment on the town was a powerful one: those who leave can never find it again, and those who find it can never leave. But Rooftrellen did not mind. The forest was his home now, and he would protect it with his life. He is the Treant Protector, guardian of the woods.

title: Troll Warlord
description: It's an easy thing to offend a troll. A prickly and contentious race, trolls thrive on argument and strife, missing no excuse to raise their voices in dispute. Males grow to maturity in subterranean chambers beneath their matriarch's lair, and when she calls for mates, the males gather in tournament to vie for her attention. Fights break out, and the combat grows increasingly chaotic until one of the males, invariably the strongest or most cunning, prevails. The victor claims a brief reign, and the matriarch begins the process of gestation. When the new offspring reach suitable age, the males either attempt to claim the matriarch again or disperse to find new holdings and mates of their own. Jah'rakal was an unusual troll. Born with a berserker's blood, he was ever eager to raise his fists and bare his fangs. He fought before he could speak, and when others of his generation gathered to mate, Jah'rakal set out to conquer. He crossed the Stonetalon Mountains, descended into the lawless outlands, and claimed a hilltribe as his own. He defeated the knights of an elven citadel, burned their forest, and fathered children on the survivors. He led a night raid on a dwarf foundry, melting down their anvil to forge a mace sized for a troll. He is Jah'rakal, the Troll Warlord, and he bows to no creature--not even his matriarch.

title: Tusk
description: It had been a brawl to remember. There stood Ymir, the Tusk, the Terror from the Barrier, the Snowball from Cobalt, the only fighter to have bested the Bristled Bruiser in a fair fight, and now the last man standing in Wolfsden Tavern. He had beaten the huge fighters from the north, the beasts from the east, and the giants from the south. He had fended off every challenger, smashed every mug, and emptied every cask. The great Nordrum the Giant Killer lay senseless on the floor, his legendary club snapped in two like a twig. The Wisp-King of Augur had fled after a single punch. Even the monstrous Dire Boar of Legend had been bested, its great tusks shattered, its terrible mouth foaming in rage as it fled. Ymir surveyed the heap of broken chairs and tables, splintered barrels, and groaning combatants. He gave a great bellow of laughter and drained another tankard. 'Come then!' he roared. 'Who else will test their mettle against the Tusk!' The Wolfsden crowd roared their approval, but none stepped forward. 'Is that all!' Ymir shouted. 'Another drink, then, and I'm off!' But as he reached for his tankard, a deep voice spoke from the doorway. 'I'll have a go.' The tavern fell silent. Ymir turned. There stood a small, runty fellow, pale and sickly to the eye. 'Hah! You? I'd hit you, and you'd fly into the wall, breaking every bone on impact!' The stranger smiled. 'That sounds like a wager. Care to put money on it?' Ymir's laughter shook the rafters. 'A bet it is! Ten thousand on the table!' The stranger shook his head. 'I don't want your money. Let's make it more interesting. If I win, you serve as my second, and follow my lead. If I lose, I'll serve you.' Ymir's laughter grew. 'Done!' He stepped forward, fist back for a swing. But as he threw his punch, the stranger... changed. His skin rippled, and his form grew to match Ymir's. His fists became identical to Ymir's. Even his face twisted to match Ymir's own bewildered expression. The stranger's fist shot forward, mirroring Ymir's blow. The punches landed simultaneously. Ymir felt his own prodigious strength crash into his jaw, just as his fist connected with the stranger. The stranger reeled, and Ymir tasted blood. But as Ymir moved in to follow up, the stranger changed again. Now it was not Ymir he faced--it was the Dire Boar of Legend. The boar's terrible tusks struck him low, and the creature's foaming mouth bit deep into his arm. Ymir fell back, and the boar followed, but now it was the Wisp-King of Augur, its ghostly touch draining Ymir's essence. Ymir swung wildly, but the Wisp-King was too fast. The creature shifted again, becoming Nordrum the Giant Killer, its great club swinging down. Ymir caught the club in his fist, but now the stranger was the Nordrum's club itself, hard as iron, and Ymir's hand went numb from the impact. Ymir staggered, and the stranger was the club no longer--now it was a swarm of Cobalt Snowballs, rolling around him, chilling his flesh. Ymir fell to one knee, and the stranger resumed his true form. 'Enough!' Ymir gasped. 'I yield!' The stranger smiled. 'A wise choice.' He helped Ymir to his feet. 'I am Tusk, and I have a feeling this is the start of a beautiful friendship.'

title: Underlord
description: Neither myth nor song exist to tell of their origin, yet it is said the great Underlord Vrogros was one of the first of the abyssal demons to crawl forth from the outer dark. He made his first incursion into the material plane not through a rend in the veil, but by using his own blood to permanently corrupt the Wellspring of Power--a fount of arcane magic that lies buried beneath the most ancient ziggurat of the forsaken city of Aziyog. From this act, the Wellspring was forever infused with evil, and all who drew from its magics would find their spells tainted by Vrogros' influence. So too would the Underlord draw power from the Wellspring, using it to summon armies of abyssal brethren to serve under his banner and fight in the legion wars. Now, after centuries of servitude, Vrogros has thrown off his bonds and risen to claim his own piece of the world above. From the sulfurous cavern known as the Rift, he emerges each night to spread the corruption of the abyss to every corner of the world. Those who fall under his sway do not become mindless servants, but rather slaves to their own darkest desires. For Vrogros does not seek to control the souls of others directly, but to turn them toward their own basest instincts--amplifying the corruption that lies within. The depraved and desperate of the world hear the Underlord's call, and respond in droves.

title: Undying
description: How long has it been since he lost his name? The torn ruin of his mind no longer knows. Dimly he recalls armor and banners and grim-faced kin riding at his side. He remembers a battle: pain and fear as pale hands ripped open his chest. Embracing the peace that followed, he drifted toward the edge of nothingness. But as his shredded life slipped beyond mortal recall, the Nightmare snatched him from the far ether, and shackled his soul with chains of green fire. Unexpectedly, he found himself squirming back to life, thrust into a corpse not his own, the chains still binding him. He was trapped in a body of dead flesh, forced to serve the Nightmare's dark will. Now he wanders the world, a slave to the thing that drags him ever onward, knowing neither peace nor death. He is the Undying, and he brings the Dirge.

title: Venomancer
description: In the Acid Jungles of Jidi Isle, poison runs in the veins and stings in the breath of every creature that lives there. Stepping from the tree-lined murk comes Lesale, a slippery sort who prefers to do his dirty work from a distance. Part scorpion, part man, he can infuse his stings with venom or lay out traps of toxified barbs. When an enemy wanders too close, he impales it with a venomous tail strike, slowing the victim as he layers on ever more toxin. Those who draw too near find themselves stupefied and unable--or unwilling--to strike back, their will dissolved by the sting of the Venomancer.

title: Viper
description: The Viper is a vicious creature, a reptilian horror capable of thriving in the Nether Reaches' worst venomous pits. Captured and bred for its venom by the Netherdrakes, Viper proved a useful tool in subduing the belligerent subterranean races. But when the Netherdrakes were defeated by the Sentinel, the Viper was left to his own devices. Without purpose, he wandered the lands, seeking a new master. When the Mad Moon fell, Viper saw his chance. He pledged his service to the Dark Ones, offering his venom in exchange for power. With his poison upgraded by the Nether Reaches' latent energies, Viper became a powerful assassin, able to weaken enemies from afar with his toxic attacks. Those who have faced him in battle can attest to his efficacy: a single splash of poison is often all it takes to leave even the strongest foe helpless and dying.

title: Visage
description: Perched atop the entrance to the Narrow Maze sit the looming shapes of snarling gargoyles, the eternal stone watchers of the realm of the dead. None may pass who cannot prove themselves, for if they should, the living will soon be made dead, and the dead will find no peace. It is the task of the eternal watchers to separate the two, to constantly patrol the Narrow Maze and ensure that none of the undead return to the realm of life. Of all these watchers, Visage is the oldest, and the most feared. He has born witness to ages come and go, and he knows the names of all who have passed through the maze. Those who hear his screeching cry know that their time has come, and that Visage has come to collect their souls for the Narrow Maze.

title: Void Spirit
description: From the Informational Plane, Inai emerges - the Void Spirit, eldest brother to the fundamental forces that bind existence. Manipulating the relationships of those who are careless enough to cross his path, he steps between planes to strike down foes and protect secrets. Those who witness his reality-shattering attacks find their minds swimming with impossible recollections. Was it one man who assaulted them... or four? Did he appear from nowhere, or step out from a rift that suddenly vanished? The Void Spirit cares not for the answers to such questions. He is concerned only with the maintenance of the great cycle - the ebb and flow of universal forces. And he will do all that is necessary to ensure its continuance.

title: Warlock
description: As Chief Curator and Head of Acquisition for the Arcane Archives of the Ultimyr Academy, Demnok Lannik possessed no remarkable mage-talent himself, but had an eye for magical antiquities of great power. Ignoring the warnings of his superiors, he opened a long-sealed vault containing the fabled collection of Dragonus, the Dragon Mage. Eager to study the draconic artifacts within, Demnok was unprepared when a book flew from the pile and struck him in the head. It was no ordinary volume, but the Book of Summoning, a tome bound in dragon hide and inscribed in dragon's blood, used by Dragonus to summon his demonic servant, the Golem. Freed from its prison, the Golem emerged in a burst of hellfire, instantly incinerating everything in the vault. Only Demnok remained, spared by the book still clutched in his hands. In shock, he turned the pages and saw that the final incantation had been altered. The Dragon Mage's death curse had been transformed into a curse of eternal life. Now bound to the book, Demnok would wield the Golem in battle, spreading hellfire and chaos wherever the Ultimyr Academy demanded. But secretly, he plots to one day turn the Golem upon the Academy, and make himself its true master.

title: Weaver
description: The fabric of creation needs constant care, lest it grow tattered; for when it unravels, whole worlds come undone. It is the work of the Weavers to keep the fabric tight, to repair worn spots in the mesh of reality. They also defend from the things that gnaw and lay their eggs in frayed regions, whose young can quickly devour an entire universe if the Weavers let their attention lapse. Skitskurr was a master Weaver, charged with keeping time and space tightly woven and in proper alignment. But his vigil ended with shameful failure when he fell asleep at his post. While he slumbered, the bonds of reality weakened, and a dark presence slipped through the gap. When Skitskurr awoke, he found his fellow Weavers devoured, and the cosmic fabric in tatters. Filled with grief and guilt, he set out to repair the damage, but the harm was too great. The dark presence had already begun to unravel the threads of creation. Skitskurr had no choice but to flee, seeking a place where he could hide and gather his strength. He found a small, out-of-the-way world, where time flowed slowly, and the fabric was still tight. There he settled, and began to weave anew. But the dark presence followed him, and now Skitskurr must fight to protect his new home, weaving spells to mend the fabric, and using his silk to bind his enemies. For if the dark presence devours this world, Skitskurr will have nowhere left to run.

title: Windranger
description: The western forests guard their secrets well. One of these is Lyralei, master archer of the wood, and favored godchild of the wind. Known now as Windranger, Lyralei 's family was killed in a storm on the night of her birth—their house blown down by the gale, contents scattered to the winds. Only the newborn survived among the debris field of death and destruction. In the quiet after the storm, the wind itself took notice of the lucky infant crying in the grass. The wind pitied the child and cradled her in its loving breeze, and so it raised her as its own, carrying her in gusts and zephyrs, adopting her as a stepchild. In the whispering wind of the trees Lyralei learned to fire her arrows true. The wind, which she called Windranger, taught her its secrets, and in return, in times of calm, Lyralei would amuse her friend with her skill and cunning. But on one fateful day, the wind was deceived by an evil mage, who tricked her into bearing him to a place of great treasure. When the wind arrived, the mage bound her with a spell and stole her voice, leaving her mute and unable to defend herself. Lyralei, seeing her friend in danger, fired a single arrow that pierced the mage's heart. The wind, freed, fled back to the west, leaving Lyralei alone in her grief. Now she wanders the plains, a bow on her back, an empty quiver at her side, friendless and unable to speak, longing to find the thief of wind and voice, and make him pay with his life.

title: Winter Wyvern
description: Like many great poets, Auroth just wants time to write, but the Winter Wyvern's life is full of interruptions. The epics of the Eldwurms have a long tradition, but the Eldwurms are a dying breed, and there are rival poets who seek to claim Auroth's place as preeminent living author. These lesser wordsmiths are nothing to a dragon of her stature, but they are persistent, and it takes no small effort to track them down and savor their smug words before consuming the author. The distractions are vexing, but Auroth's genius abides, and her memories hold the full texts of her masterwork epics, even if her life is too busy for new composition. Some say it's a pity she doesn't recite her works aloud. But when enemies come calling, Auroth takes wing and answers, and her frigid voice speaks lines of epic verse that will never be written down.

title: Witch Doctor
description: A wiry silhouette hitches forward—uneven of feature and limb, bizarre of gait, relentlessly criss-crossing the battlefield in search of that vital weak point where his talents can do most good, and most harm. Whether broken or mismade it is not clear, but still, none can doubt the power carried in his twisted physique. A long staff thumps the earth as Zharvakko the Witch Doctor advances, deploying a terrifying arsenal of fetishes, hexes and potions. It is a body of magical knowledge learned and perfected over several lifetimes in the island highlands of Arktura, now wielded with precision accuracy against his enemies. Zharvakko can be your best friend or your worst enemy--healing allies and laying waste to all who oppose him.

title: Wraith King
description: For untold years the Wraith King ruled his land with an iron fist. He had emerged from the ancient fog beyond the Wailing Wall as a champion of the afterlife, his skin cloaked in the ash of the dead. No one knew how long he had dwelt there in the dark swamp known as the Blighted Land. But by some mystic art he had bound his life-force to the realm of the living, and death could not claim him. Whenever he was wounded, his skin would knit together. When struck down, he rose again. His subjects, wrapped in awe by his seeming immortality, followed him unquestioningly. Thus he became arrogant, taunting death even as he bound himself ever more closely to it. He laughed when the plague came, for he thought it could not touch him. But the plague was no ordinary sickness. It was the Finger of Death, sent to usher mortals to their ends. One by one his subjects died, until his kingdom was nothing but a wasteland of the wretched dead. Still he would not cross over. Starved and rotted, his flesh reduced to little more than bone, he was a king without a people. But when the Finger came for him at last, he realized his folly. Too late. He had thought himself beyond death's reach, but now he saw that death had only prolonged his suffering. With a desolate wail he surrendered to oblivion, and was finally taken. Yet in the land of the dead, he found...nothing. An endless nothing. His kingdom was not there. He was a king without a kingdom once more. And now he is filled with wrath, and roams the world seeking retribution against the living, for the crime of still being alive while he wanders without end. For the Wraith King, nothing less than an apocalypse will satisfy his anger, and to that end he is prepared to fight until every last soul has joined him in the deadlands.

title: Zeus
description: Lord of Heaven, father of gods, Zeus treats all the Heroes as if they are his rambunctious, rebellious children. After being caught unnumbered times in the midst of trysts with countless mortal women, his divine wife finally gave him an ultimatum: 'If you love mortals so much, go and become one. If you can prove yourself faithful, then return to me as my husband. Otherwise, go and die among your creations.' Zeus found her logic (and her magic) irresistible, and agreed to her plan. He has been on his best behavior ever since, being somewhat fonder of immortality than he is of mortals. But to prove himself worthy of his eternal spouse, he must continue to pursue victory on the field of battle.
